item.title: Kid Rock’s Nashville Bar Denies Wrongdoing In Patron’s Assault Lawsuit
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Kid Rock's Nashville bar disputes a patron's claims that security guards injured him after an encounter with a musician.
item.content:encoded:
Kid Rock‘s Nashville bar is disputing a customer’s lawsuit alleging security guards injured him after he touched a performer’s guitar. Joshua Welch is suing the establishment, not the musician personally.

Welch says the confrontation happened in December 2025, according to TMZ. His lawyer describes the initial contact with the instrument as a light touch with one finger.

A guard began escorting him out, and Welch allegedly reached toward the guitar again as he left. He claims three men subsequently attacked him inside an elevator before throwing him out at ground level.

Welch says the confrontation left him with an injured right hand after he repeatedly tried to get back up. The ring finger injury required surgery about a month later, according to his account.

The reported claims include assault and battery, negligence, negligent hiring and training, and false imprisonment. The restaurant denies wrongdoing and maintains that its security staff was justified in using force.

The venue advertises space for nearly 2,000 people across its multiple levels in downtown Nashville. Its public-facing identity combines live performances and a steakhouse under Kid Rock’s name.

The business trades on the entertainer’s name in one of Nashville’s busiest live-music districts. Its own website describes a five-floor property at Third Avenue and Broadway with four stages and six bars.

The first floor and mezzanine overlook a two-story main stage where musicians perform daily, according to the venue. Its rooftop provides another gathering area above the downtown entertainment strip.

Kid Rock has previously distinguished his public association with the restaurant from running its daily operations. AllHipHop reported his response in May 2025 after staffing concerns tied to immigration enforcement brought scrutiny to the business.

That earlier controversy concerned reports that kitchen workers had been sent home during immigration enforcement activity in Nashville. His response addressed operational responsibility, not the separate customer encounter now described in Welch’s lawsuit.

The venue also drew emergency crews on March 17, 2026, when flames were spotted in its ductwork. Nashville firefighters received the call around 11:15 A.M., with no injuries reported in that incident.

The establishment lists its downtown Nashville address as 221 Broadway on its official website.

item.title: YNW Melly Seeks To Keep Gang Testimony Out Of Murder Retrial
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: YNW Melly challenges the gang testimony prosecutors want jurors to hear as his defense prepares for another murder trial.
item.content:encoded:
YNW Melly wants jurors kept away from gang testimony, his lawyers say, which never explained the killings prosecutors have charged him with.

His defense is asking a Broward County judge to exclude gang evidence and related expert testimony from his double-murder retrial.

Attorneys Carey Haughwout and Drew Findling filed the eight-page motion November 13. Their argument targets the gap between describing an alleged gang affiliation and proving the murders served a gang’s interests.

“The gang-related evidence at the first trial was lengthy, prejudicial, and, most importantly, bore no connection to the alleged murders,” the defense wrote.

The lawyers focus on Detective Polo’s earlier testimony about the Bloods and G-Shine, including their origins, rules and hierarchy. They say he interpreted photographs, conversations and symbols without tying that material to the charged shootings.

“However, at no point did Detective Polo connect the gang-related evidence to the allegations in this case,” the defense wrote.

Prosecutors have argued that gang evidence helps explain motive and intent. The defense filing quotes the state’s response to an earlier motion as calling it “directly relevant to the State’s theory of the case regarding motive and intent, regardless of potential sentence.”

The new request also leans on an earlier evidence ruling. According to the defense, Judge John Murphy’s December 20, 2023 order already excluded most gang-related digital material, including emails, text messages and expert interpretations of those records.

Melly faces two first-degree murder charges in the October 26, 2018 deaths of fellow rappers YNW Sakchaser and YNW Juvy. Prosecutors allege the men were shot inside a vehicle before the scene was staged as a drive-by shooting.

Melly has pleaded not guilty. His first trial ended with a deadlocked jury in July 2023, and prosecutors are seeking the death penalty if he is convicted.

The evidentiary fight comes as his team continues preparing for the retrial. The indictment includes an allegation that the killings benefited, promoted or furthered a criminal gang, which the defense argues cannot justify unrelated testimony about gang culture. The motion warns that broad descriptions of gang practices could encourage jurors to judge Melly through stereotypes.

Jury selection is scheduled to begin January 6, 2027.

item.title: LL Cool J Takes “NCIS: New York” Into More Than 135 Markets
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: LL Cool J adds a worldwide TV win as buyers pick up his Sam Hanna spinoff across streaming services and broadcasters.
item.content:encoded:
LL Cool J has overseas broadcasters buying into his latest run as Sam Hanna on “NCIS: New York.” The series has secured distribution agreements covering more than 135 markets worldwide.

Skydance Global Content Sales announced the agreements on Monday.

“It’s exciting to introduce the next iteration of the NCIS universe to the entire world. I can’t wait for people to see what we do with these stories and how we take the world on a guided tour of parts of New York they’ve never seen before,” LL Cool J said.

He’s starring in the series and also serves as an executive producer.

That producer credit follows decades of screen work. Before Sam Hanna, LL Cool J carried the sitcom “In the House,” beginning in 1995. His film roles stretched from “Toys” to “Deep Blue Sea” and Oliver Stone’s football drama “Any Given Sunday.” He later shared the screen with Queen Latifah in “Last Holiday,” moving between comedy, drama and action.

Hanna’s new assignment follows more than a decade of television cases in California. LL Cool J played Hanna through 14 seasons of “NCIS: Los Angeles,” which ran from 2009 until 2023. Even after that series ended, he kept Hanna active through “NCIS: Hawai’i” and appearances on the original “NCIS.”

He also learned the business beyond acting. Alongside his scripted roles, he hosted and produced “Lip Sync Battle” and executive produced the documentary series “Story of Cool.” The competition series earned Emmy and Producers Guild nominations. New York adds a scripted franchise to that producing resume.

For this spinoff, his involvement went beyond agreeing to return as Hanna. LL Cool J told TV Insider he brought in former “NCIS: Los Angeles” showrunner R. Scott Gemmill to help develop the new series. That put him into the project’s development, not simply its cast.

AllHipHop covered the New York spinoff’s green light in April, when Scott Caan joined the project following his own long run on “Hawaii Five-0.” This time, Hanna’s working in the city where the character grew up, rather than returning to his old Los Angeles assignment.

Byron Balasco serves as showrunner on the CBS Studios production.

item.title: Lil Baby Tops Hip-Hop Albums Chart As FRESH Opens With 59,000 Units
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Lil Baby claims another genre-chart crown while FRESH's confirmed first-week total falls below WHAM's opening numbers.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Baby has the final first-week numbers for FRESH, and they put him atop the R&B/Hip-Hop albums chart without delivering another No. 1 on the all-genre Billboard 200.

The album enters at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 with 59,000 equivalent album units, according to Billboard. The total covers U.S. activity from November 6 through November 12, not just copies purchased.

Streaming accounts for 55,000 of those units, compared with 4,000 from album sales. Listeners generated 56.8 million official on-demand streams across the project’s songs during that opening week.

There is another win beyond the album ranking: “Dead Fresh” finally reaches No. 1 on Hot Rap Songs in its 17th week. The single spent 14 nonconsecutive weeks at No. 2 behind Drake’s “Janice STFU” before making the move.

FRESH becomes Lil Baby’s fifth leader on Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums. His earlier chart-toppers were My Turn, the Lil Durk collaboration The Voice Of The Heroes, It’s Only Me and WHAM.

The new figures also settle the question raised by an early forecast AllHipHop covered while the tracking week was still underway. That estimate pointed toward more than 60,000 units and left a potential No. 1 finish open.

For comparison, WHAM opened with 140,000 units in 2025, including 50,000 album sales. Its launch included a paid expanded version with four additional songs before those tracks became available to stream the following week. That makes the new album’s opening total 81,000 units lower, with the gap in full-album purchases accounting for 46,000 of that difference.

Lil Baby released FRESH on November 6 with 17 tracks. Future and Young Thug join Rylo Rodriguez on “All My Partnas,” while Rylo returns for “In Your Head.” The production credits also bring together Metro Boomin and London on Da Track, alongside Pharrell Williams, giving the album several familiar collaborators behind its mostly solo tracklist.

The rollout began months before the album arrived. Pharrell Williams produced “Dead Fresh,” which Lil Baby introduced at Louis Vuitton’s menswear show in Paris in June before taking the song into the album campaign.

Lil Baby’s Fresh Prince Of Atlanta birthday concert is scheduled for December 5 at State Farm Arena.

item.title: Chrisean Rock Adam22 “Should Be Scared” After Years Of Disrespect
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Chrisean Rock explains her clash with Adam22 on Kick as his statements about police and possible legal action continue.
item.content:encoded:
Chrisean Rock says her confrontation with Adam22 followed years of disrespect, offering her own explanation after he said he would involve police.

The rapper and reality personality addressed the encounter during a Kick stream. She described his comments about her as bullying and said she wouldn’t accept it face-to-face.

“Somebody try to bully me…you know what I’m going to do, I’m going to fight back,” she said. “You can’t bully me.”

Rock said she had previously ignored his remarks instead of answering them publicly. In her account, having him direct the comments at her in person changed how she responded.

She also warned Adam22, “You should be scared,” while arguing that people should not assume their comments will go unanswered in person.

The November 12 encounter took place at Wild ‘N Out Live at Intuit Dome in Inglewood, California. Adam22 mocked her parenting during the show, and she struck him.

Her stream adds her explanation to a dispute that has already produced several public statements from Adam22. It does not establish what police will do with his complaint.

As AllHipHop reported Monday, the No Jumper founder said he had visited the Inglewood Police Department after announcing plans to report her. He also predicted that she would be arrested.

That prediction was his own. The report did not include an arrest warrant or a police report, and his statements about a potential lawsuit did not establish that he had filed a civil case.

Before discussing his police visit, Adam22 had raised concerns about the impact on his work. He said the swelling in his jaw mattered because his job requires lengthy stretches of talking on camera.

In earlier coverage, he described recording sessions that could run for several hours and suggested the injury might interfere with that schedule. Those were his descriptions of the discomfort and possible consequences, not a documented assessment of lost earnings.

The confrontation followed an existing public disagreement between them rather than a first encounter over a single joke. Adam22 described the event as a comedy battle in which personal insults were exchanged.

Rock addressed the incident on Kick.

item.title: Will Smith’s Former Friend Claims He Grabbed His Crotch In New Lawsuit, Actor Denies It
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Will Smith pushes back as Bilaal Salaam brings a sexual battery lawsuit amid ongoing legal fights involving his family.
item.content:encoded:
Will Smith is denying a sexual battery allegation from former friend Bilaal Salaam, who has brought a new lawsuit against him.

“This claim is false. It never happened,” Smith’s lawyer told TMZ. The attorney also accused Salaam of repeatedly making false statements about Smith and his family and said they would fight him in court.

Salaam places the alleged incident at a Hollywood after-party following the 2019 premiere of “Aladdin.”

He claims Smith grabbed his genitals over his clothing and that he pushed the actor away. He says the alleged contact lasted about 10 seconds before he objected loudly.

The lawsuit also describes an earlier exchange while the two recorded a video together. Salaam says Smith made comments about his body that left him embarrassed.

According to TMZ’s account of the filing, Salaam alleges Smith apologized and later approached him again with Jada Pinkett Smith. Salaam claims Smith asked him to keep quiet about what happened.

TMZ published the allegation and the attorney’s denial together in its report on Tuesday.

Salaam and the Smith family were already involved in litigation over a separate alleged confrontation. Salaam’s $3 million case against Jada concerns threats he claims she made at a birthday gathering for Smith in 2021.

Jada has denied wrongdoing and challenged portions of that lawsuit. Salaam has described emotional distress and damage to his reputation, while Jada has disputed his allegations through court filings.

That dispute has already produced rulings over legal fees and efforts to involve Smith. Salaam previously sought to question Smith under oath and tried to add him as a defendant in the case against Jada.

Another member of Smith’s family took legal action against Salaam earlier this year. Sheree Zampino, Smith’s former wife, filed a complaint in Los Angeles County Superior Court on May 27.

Zampino accused Salaam of slander and intentional infliction of emotional distress over an online interview. She alleged that his statements about her were false and sought more than $1 million in compensatory damages.

Jada previously obtained an order requiring Salaam to pay $32,836 in attorney fees and costs.

item.title: Yung Miami Eyes Tour & Gets Key To Miami-Dade County
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Yung Miami says a tour and possible Caresha Please return are among her next goals following the release of Watch Dis.
item.content:encoded:
Yung Miami is looking beyond her solo album, with a tour in development and a possible return for Caresha Please on her list.

Local 10 News reported that she wants to release more music while exploring those next steps. The report did not announce tour dates or a podcast premiere.

“Yeah, I want to be a mogul,” she told reporter Alexis Frazier. “I want the moon, the stars, the sun. If I can, I want everything.”

Frazier spoke with the rapper at Sweat Records, where supporters gathered to celebrate her accomplishments. Local 10 reported that she received a key to Miami-Dade County, with October 23 designated in her honor.

The next step also comes with her first Grammy nomination. “Spend Dat” is up for Best Rap Song at the 2027 awards, a songwriting category that credits her alongside three collaborators.

The podcast would bring her back to a platform she built before this solo album arrived. Caresha Please launched in 2022 and accumulated more than 45 million YouTube views.

The nomination follows months of backlash over lyrics critics said celebrated scamming and shoplifting. India.Arie challenged the song’s message, while Brownstone’s Nicci Gilbert said she would use her Grammy vote against it. Uncle Luke and Trick Daddy defended Yung Miami during the dispute.

Watch Dis arrived October 23 through Uptown Records after two years of work, according to the announcement. Its 21 tracks include Summer Walker, Bryson Tiller, Travis Scott, Quavo and G Herbo. Walker appears on “Ride For You,” another collaboration on the project.

The album also puts her hometown collaborators together on “Dade County,” featuring Rick Ross, Trick Daddy and Trina. The track list pairs that regional lineup with the more personal “Dear JT.”

Her breakout single had already raised expectations. As AllHipHop previously reported, Yung Miami said the success of “Spend Dat” made her revisit the album and sharpen the work before release.

She described feeling both excitement and anxiety as the record grew. The single reached No. 17 on the Billboard Hot 100 and earned platinum certification.

The Grammy ceremony takes place February 7, 2027, in Los Angeles.

item.title: Meek Mill Calls For His Own Awards Show As He Challenges Streaming
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Meek Mill called for an artist-run awards show while pushing rappers to build their own platforms and challenge streaming.
item.content:encoded:
Meek Mill wants an artist-run awards show as he pushes rappers to take more control of their music businesses.

The Philadelphia rapper floated the idea on X while arguing that artists need alternatives to streaming platforms and traditional label arrangements. His awards proposal followed a discussion about how upcoming rappers find listeners and whether established services give them enough exposure.

“We starting our own award show too that’s enough …. they just bullying us now lol,” Meek wrote.

The conversation also included Doe Boy, who pointed to LiveMixtapes, Spinrilla and MyMixtapez as examples of platforms that helped listeners discover rappers. He argued that a new service should prioritize finding emerging talent.

“Apple Music and Spotify not really for discovering artist, we need something that can help upcoming rappers get seen!” Doe Boy posted. Meek responded by urging artists to create their own apps and websites rather than depend entirely on placement elsewhere.

In that response, Meek complained about the difficulty of getting onto playlists and generating enough streams. He also argued that strong numbers do not necessarily make collecting earnings from a label easy.

Meek then proposed a meeting bringing technology and Hip-Hop together to discuss how streaming affects musicians and their audiences. He wanted the conversation to produce improvements for both groups without abandoning the possibility of making money.

Those complaints continue a long-running concern for Meek, who previously questioned what he earned from his Drake collaboration “Going Bad.” At the time, he said he had been told the record generated $24 million but could not get a clear answer about his own share.

Meek is also scheduled to bring Dream Chasers Nights to Philadelphia’s Xfinity Mobile Arena on November 24.

item.title: LeekOnnaComeUp Killed In Baltimore Triple Shooting
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: LeekOnnaComeUp's catalog spans years of independent releases as Baltimore detectives seek tips about Sunday's gunfire.
item.content:encoded:
LeekOnnaComeUp died in Sunday’s Baltimore shooting, according to CBS Baltimore, which identified the rapper.

Baltimore police are investigating the November 15 gunfire on the 5400 block of Reisterstown Road. Officers responded around 2:42 P.M. and found a wounded 41-year-old man.

Two other victims reached a hospital separately. In their Monday update, police said a 26-year-old man had died, and a 21-year-old man remained critically injured. The oldest victim had injuries that were not considered life-threatening.

“Homicide detectives responded to the scene and have assumed control of the investigation,” the department said in its incident report.

LeekOnnaComeUp’s catalog includes 5605, an eight-track project released April 24. Apple Music lists its running time at 17 minutes and credits the release to the artist.

His earlier projects include Reality, released in 2019, and Come Up 101, which followed in 2020. He also released Leeky Cage 5 in 2025.

His newest releases show an artist who was still putting out music this fall. Bc Tae’s “Blood Money,” featuring LeekOnnaComeUp and ABG Lorr Tyy, arrived November 6. That collaboration came just nine days before the shooting, adding another guest appearance to a catalog built through solo projects and work with other artists.

He had also released Leeky Cage 6 on August 28. The ten-track album followed April’s 5605, with Bc Tae appearing on the interlude and OcuCam joining him on “Ina While.” It continued the numbered series that included last year’s Leeky Cage 5.

Those collaborations extended beyond his latest album. His six-track Recovery EP, released June 17, 2025, included Dai Money and Lor Melly on “448,” Ocu Cam on “Im Sorry,” and Worldwide JP on “Love Don’t Live Here.” In 2020, he teamed with NLU YoungNickk for “RockStar LifeStyle,” an earlier example of his work alongside other performers. The EP ran just over 13 minutes, with those collaborations spread across half of its tracks.

Baltimore previously lost rapper Lor Scoota and his manager to separate fatal shootings in 2016.

Anyone with information about Sunday’s shooting can contact homicide detectives at 410-396-2100 or anonymously reach Metro Crime Stoppers at 1-866-7LOCKUP.

item.title: Ice Spice Fuels Latto Beef Rumors After Instagram Unfollow
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: Ice Spice’s cryptic insult has fans questioning her relationship with Latto after a reported Instagram unfollow.
item.content:encoded:
Ice Spice has the internet wondering whether her apparent truce with Latto already needs a refund.

I noticed – after thousands of fans – Latto reportedly unfollowed the Bronx rapper on Instagram, and suddenly everybody became a forensic investigator with unlimited screen time. Then came a message from Ice that made the situation considerably less friendly. According to published reports, both rappers were no longer following each other when the latest chatter picked up.

Ice posted:

“Aww pu**y what happened”

Ice Spice dropped that comment on X…she did not name Latto. But you know she was talking about her. We are not stupid.

These two gave everybody reason to believe they could coexist quite comfortably.

They collaborated on “Gyatt” in 2025 and appeared together on Kai Cenat’s stream. A joint record generally suggests you can at least tolerate somebody long enough to finish a video shoot. Now fans are looking at that collaboration like an old vacation photo after a breakup. 

There is another reason the wording has attracted attention. Fans have connected Ice’s insult to the earlier leaked phone call controversy involving Cardi B. It was at that time that Latto was disparaged. Oh well.

My question is simple: did something actually happen between these women? We do not know, but I have a follow-up rumor that will make this even more messy. Stand by and buckle up.

One more time…
